claims.text: Pronounced atomic lattice distortions in single-phase HEAs enhance dynamic load partitioning.
Atomic lattice distortions locally impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion increases dynamic yield strength while preserving ductility relative to conventional alloys.
Atomic-size mismatches among multiple principal elements induce measurable lattice distortions in the proposed HEA.
A conventional alloy with similar overall chemistry but lower configurational complexity will have reduced lattice distortion.
Matching temperature, strain rate, and environmental conditions isolates the effect of lattice distortion.
Localized lattice distortions create heterogeneous internal stress fields.
The heterogeneous internal stress fields affect dislocation nucleation and mobility.
Lattice distortions act as dynamic obstacles to dislocation glide and increase dislocation pinning.
Increased dislocation pinning promotes a more heterogeneous strain distribution.
Heterogeneous strain partitioning enhances work hardening and permits ductility to be maintained under dynamic loading.
Under high-strain-rate loading, the HEA will have higher dynamic yield strength than the baseline conventional alloy.
Under high-strain-rate loading, the HEA will maintain or improve ductility relative to the baseline conventional alloy.
The proposed mechanism is expected to operate in single-phase HEAs from ambient to moderately elevated temperatures.
The mechanism is expected to operate predominantly at strain rates where dynamic effects on dislocation motion are significant.
The mechanism may not hold at very low strain rates, in multiphase materials, or at temperatures where phase transformations occur.
The qualitative trend of increased dynamic strength with maintained ductility is supported by prior evidence.
Processing-induced grain-size differences or precipitates may affect the magnitude of the predicted behavior.
In situ high-energy X-ray diffraction or transmission electron microscopy can be used to monitor dislocation behavior and local strain distributions during dynamic testing.

Failure to observe increased dynamic yield strength together with lattice-distortion-associated dislocation pinning, or observing similar behavior without significant distortion, would falsify the hypothesis.
